concepts.definition: The engineering Ontology is the single semantic truth of a designed boundary. Diagrams, matrices, IACS, APIs, operation registers, SDK/CLI surfaces, schemas, codecs, manifests, catalogues, target architecture, modules and proof inventories preserve it through the specified design and requirement paths; they are not independent semantic authorities.

grounding.quote: The Ontology is one semantic truth

concepts.label: Engineering Ontology

concepts.definition: A smallest parameterised atomic-function family derived by the Ontology to make entity lifecycles logically complete. Its derivation evidence relates discovered functionality, entity, atomic function or template, higher-order composition, effect class, required authority and disposition.

grounding.quote: | Discovered functionality | Entity | Atomic function or template | Higher-order composition | Effect class | Required authority | Disposition |

concepts.label: Atomic function family

conditions: The boundary has higher-order behaviour.
concepts.definition: A declared governing composition and effect algebra. Typical categories are unit/lift, sequential composition, parallel/applicative composition, fold/evaluation, retry/recovery, recursion/fixed point and projection.

grounding.quote:
Typical categories include unit
or lift, sequential composition, parallel or applicative composition, fold
or evaluation, retry or recovery, recursion or fixed point, and
projection.

concepts.label: Higher-order composition

concepts.definition: One irreducible semantic design relation: atomic-function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation, topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot honestly be composed from other accepted atoms while preserving meaning. Prime is decided at semantic-design altitude.

grounding.quote:
A Prime semantic atom is one irreducible design relation: an atomic
function family, identity, authority transition, lifecycle relation,
topology, effect, closure law or composition law that cannot be expressed
honestly by composing other accepted atoms while preserving the same
meaning

concepts.label: Prime semantic atom

concepts.definition: Design review of the complete candidate semantic-atom family and every proposed realisation projection, including all identities, authority transitions, lifecycle relations, topologies, functions, composition laws, effects and closure laws. Individual plausibility or a function-and-carrier-only pass does not establish whole-family Prime.

grounding.quote:
Prime review evaluates the complete candidate semantic-atom family and
every proposed realisation projection, not only functions, carriers or
each atom in isolation.

concepts.label: Whole-family Prime contraction

concepts.definition: A realisation projection implements accepted semantic atoms. Prime-conformance applies to functions, classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules; source-code size and one-to-one atom correspondence are immaterial.

grounding.quote:
Prime-conformance applies to these realisation projections: functions,
classes, carrier types, top-level schema records and modules.

concepts.label: Realisation projection

concepts.definition: The Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set is the smallest lawful top-level carrier family carrying a boundary's real functionality and authority flow. Example roles are source truth, admission, execution, yield/recovery, effect plan and public projection. It is an Ontology projection and declared carrier inventory, not an origin or replacement of semantic meaning.

grounding.quote:
The IACS is the smallest
set of carriers required to carry the real functionality and authority
flow of the boundary.

concepts.label: Irreducible Architectural Carrier Set

concepts.definition: Payload detail inside a boundary that is not top-level by default.

grounding.quote:
- Subordinate Payload: payload detail that exists inside that boundary but
  is not top-level by default;

concepts.label: Subordinate Payload

concepts.definition: The explicit test preceding a Subordinate Payload's promotion to a top-level architectural type, including class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record.

grounding.quote:
A top-level class, dataclass, TypedDict, enum or named schema record
justifies its existence as an architectural boundary, not merely as
payload detail

concepts.label: Promotion Test

concepts.definition: Design debt in which payload detail becomes peer types because typing feels difficult; internal records become public schema without a new authoritative boundary; near-identical top-level types proliferate where one carrier family suffices; or one migration silently becomes parallel schema migrations.

grounding.quote:
Boundary Inflation is design debt, not
progress

concepts.label: Boundary Inflation

conditions: A realisation derives from an existing design line, released tenant or reference implementation.
concepts.definition: A derivation chain through constitutional WHAT, reference design, target Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping, target design mapping, target module boundary assets and implementation. It prevents incidental reference drift, delivery quirks, helper sprawl and accidental authority paths from being imported without an audit trail.

grounding.quote:
The required derivation
evidence is: (1) constitutional WHAT; (2) reference design; (3) target
Ontology and reference-to-Ontology mapping; (4) target design mapping; (5)
target module boundary assets; (6) implementation.

concepts.label: Reference-derived module design

concepts.definition: One complete design asset comprising distinct domain, execution and lifecycle views, normally Mermaid classDiagram, sequenceDiagram and stateDiagram-v2. These are fidelity-checked Ontology projections and together the sign-off surface for domain identity, authority, behaviour, lifecycle and axiom conformance.
concepts.label: Three-view design asset

conditions: An accepted material-frame basis and a proposed bounded action are given.
concepts.definition: The sufficiency property of selected method basis plus accepted design for recovering every governing relation in an action's causally closed affected set and deciding preserves, changes, duplicates or violates. Method specifies required relations and reasoning; design supplies concrete invariant values. This is durable reasoning state, not dialogue, memory, folklore or a separate documentation package.

grounding.quote:
the selected method describes which relations
are required and how to reason about them; the accepted design supplies
the concrete invariant values.

concepts.label: Invariant reconstruction sufficiency

concepts.definition: The structural Ontology projection for the active boundary, showing domain identities/cardinalities, ownership/invariants/lifecycle relationships, boundary-crossing atomic functions and inputs/outputs, shape-determining composition, IACS-to-Prime mappings, subordinate and effect-edge payloads, downstream projections, deferred families, authority and visibility, and genuine composition/containment/association/variant structure.

grounding.quote: The `classDiagram` is the structural domain projection of the Ontology

concepts.label: Domain model

concepts.definition: The behavioural projection of Ontology functions and authority, showing supported execution from admitted input to result or truthful stop, with owners and required authority for every decision, admission, execution, projection and effect boundary.

grounding.quote:
It shows the supported
execution path from admitted input to result or truthful stop, and names
the owner and required authority of every decision, admission, execution,
projection and effect boundary.

concepts.label: Sequence model

concepts.definition: The lifecycle projection of Ontology entities, covering the complete admitted lifecycle of the active boundary, including every refusal, blocked, continuation, retry, escalation and terminal state that boundary can produce.

grounding.quote:
It shows the complete admitted lifecycle for
the active boundary, including refusal, blocked, continuation, retry,
escalation and terminal states that the boundary can produce.

concepts.label: State model

concepts.definition: Design-pack assessment of each applicable product, graph, language, runtime, handler and module axiom. Minimum columns are Axiom, Ontology evidence, Authority, Domain evidence, Sequence evidence, State evidence, Native enforcement, Admission/compiler enforcement, Verdict and Gap owner. Its verdicts and direct core results are assessment data, distinct from acceptance.

grounding.quote: | Axiom | Ontology evidence | Authority | Domain evidence | Sequence evidence | State evidence | Native enforcement | Admission/compiler enforcement | Verdict | Gap owner |

concepts.label: Cross-view axiom evaluation

concepts.definition: The design authority's separate acceptance decisions for the Ontology and design pack. Each consumes availability and assessment, including decision completeness, axiom results and cross-view proofs. accepted denotes accept, mapped to satisfied for the predicate that this candidate is accepted at its declared design-gate boundary; pack production and passing assessments are not acceptance.

grounding.quote:
The Ontology verdict and the design verdict are each an acceptance
result: a decision that consumes the results of assessment, distinct from
them.

concepts.label: Ontology and design acceptance gate

conditions: A material semantic boundary is considered.
concepts.definition: A subordinate projection exposing abstract data types, identity/key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation/effect boundaries, selected implementations and domain-to-computational mappings. It reveals repeated machinery hidden by domain identities but cannot decide semantic identity, ownership or authority.

grounding.quote:
the design projects the
domain design into its computational realisation: abstract data types,
identity and key structures, algorithms, algebraic laws, mutation and
effect boundaries, selected implementations, and domain-to-computational
mappings.

concepts.label: Computational realisation projection

concepts.definition: Optional world-model justification: a Markov object is a candidate identity-bearing, stable self-bounding cut whose effective blanket separates identity-bearing from context-bearing structure. IACS analogises the smallest lawful cut; promotion asks independent boundary authority; inflation mistakes fragments for peer objects; strong boundary typing avoids fuzzy, reconstructive or controller-owned identity.

grounding.quote:
It treats a Markov object
as a candidate identity-bearing cut: a stable self-bounding pattern whose
effective blanket separates what is load-bearing for identity from what is
load-bearing for context.

concepts.label: Optional theoretical framing

conditions: The profile governs a realisation boundary.
concepts.definition: Recommended role taxonomy: carrier modules define typed immutable inputs, outputs, contracts, transitions, records or envelopes; semantic kernels transform carriers without effects; effect shells emit events, publish files, call networks/subprocesses, persist or deliver to operators; projection modules derive reports/read models from authoritative truth; adapters translate external boundaries to internal carriers without inventing law; constructors/materialisers write built/generated artifacts from admitted carriers and explicit plans. These roles bound traversal reasoning and make recurrence visible, rather than impose naming ceremony.

grounding.quote:
modules should be
classified by role

concepts.label: Module role taxonomy

concepts.definition: The profile's preferred realisation discipline uses an algebraic primitive with projections rather than multiple local decision systems, and prefers total functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds.

grounding.quote:
Projects using this profile prefer one algebraic primitive plus
projections over several local decision systems, and prefer total
functions, closed enums, explicit state and deterministic folds

concepts.label: Preferred realisation discipline

concepts.definition: A semantic function's outcomes are Product domain values, including unsupported or rejected outcomes where used. They are distinct from method results: an evaluation consuming those outcomes returns its own core result value.

grounding.quote:
The outcome values a
semantic function returns are the Product's domain values, not results of
this method; an evaluation that consumes them returns its own core value

concepts.label: Product outcome versus method result

conditions: A boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor, executor, builder or substrate.
concepts.definition: A governance surface describes state, boundary and admissible routes. Lawful publication includes current state, preserved structure, unmet pressure or unresolved identities, route eligibility, lawful edit/proof frontier, admitted policy identity and prior-turn/run continuity. Strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor should work.

grounding.quote:
Governance surfaces describe the state, boundary
and admissible routes; strategy surfaces prescribe how another actor
should do the work.

concepts.label: Governance and strategy boundary

conditions: A realisation boundary is lawfully open for migration, refactor or bounded implementation work.
concepts.definition: Boundary-local improvement subordinate to constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Examples include removing parser re-entry on locally assembled truth, consolidating local route logic, improving a local algorithm or scan, and simplifying proof fixtures/tests without changing their module claims.

grounding.quote:
This does not
outrank constitutional truth, declared module ownership evidence or
functional equivalence; it is subordinate to them.

concepts.label: Opportunistic optimisation

conditions: The same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed boundary.
concepts.definition: Review of a commonisation candidate rather than another purely local cleanup. Candidates usually are not product truth, are authority-neutral, recur across at least two tickets or module boundaries, and work through local adapters without changing semantic ownership. Typical cases include expectation derivation, nested contract/policy carriers, proof fixtures, effect-edge plans and constructors without semantic law.

grounding.quote:
When the same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed
boundary, review treats that pattern as a commonisation candidate rather
than as another purely local clean-up

concepts.label: Recurrence extraction

conditions: A ticket applies the profile to its boundary and claims that boundary has been processed.
concepts.definition: A bounded check against accepted design and the exact closure claim, reconstructing the claim's causal closure from governing requirements through Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views, target modules, implementation and module-owned proof. This is not a review of the whole Product/history or merely previous findings.

grounding.quote:
The check reconstructs the complete selected function from governing
requirements through the accepted Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views,
target modules, implementation and module-owned proof

concepts.label: Post-ticket design review

concepts.definition: An interface family has one authoritative source truth consumed by downstream interfaces. Bleed occurs when an interface reconstructs another's truth, projections decide closure, reports/prompts decide admission, wrappers decide kernel meaning or adapters invent semantics.
concepts.label: Interface family and semantic bleed

concepts.definition: A new-looking surface forwarding to old authority, reconstructing missing truth from it, keeping the old path executable under a new name, or keeping proofs green while old law governs. This is bridge debt rather than completed migration.

grounding.quote:
A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
proofs to stay green while the old law still governs.

concepts.label: Proxy interface

concepts.definition: Code review under this profile asks the 56 design questions, including semantic ownership, projection fidelity, lawful boundaries, proof, lifecycle, graph alignment and foundation selection. The source diagnoses inability to answer them cleanly as excessive coupling or imperative design.

grounding.quote:
If these questions cannot be answered cleanly, the realisation is too
coupled or too imperative

concepts.label: Design review questions

conditions: A project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation.
concepts.definition: Explicit functional realisation review, language-agnostic across module, carrier and data-entity design and implementation review, with a compact hard gate for new or materially changed boundaries and accepted-basis/no-material-delta reuse for unchanged ones.

grounding.quote:
When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks

concepts.label: Functional realisation checklist

concepts.definition: Adoption of the available design-module profile by Product authority. Inclusion in a selected method cut makes the profile available; the profile adds no adopter. Recording mechanisms include ADR/design citations, agent entry surfaces, migration-ticket review criteria and module classification.

grounding.quote:
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter.

concepts.label: Profile adoption

concepts.definition: Named divisions of responsibility: SPEC_METHOD owns constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and migration; RELEASE owns release cut, Product/install qualification and version-line/exact-cut/selector decisions; ODD owns graph-native constructive shape; DESIGN_MODULE owns preferred design and implementation structure within those boundaries; UX adds rendering, state-transition and effect-membrane discipline for UX surfaces. ASSURANCE lifecycle confirmation concerns sufficient lifecycle signal, not release eligibility or rollout.
concepts.label: Related method member roles

conditions: A consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role operates under the graph-execution profile.
concepts.definition: Default identity generators, validators and normalisers publishable for that realisation's own runtime surfaces and default ODD surface kinds used by default F_D helpers. Their default/override law is referred to IDENTITY §7.

grounding.quote:
the permission is scoped to that role
and does not extend to other runtime realisations

concepts.label: Bound-runtime identity defaults

concepts.definition: A provenance register of predecessor DESIGN_MODULE_METHOD rows and one IDENTITY_METHOD row, recording conservation, replacement proposals, receiving loci, terminology changes and new additions. Its routes are provenance only; its conservation statements are source claims, not verification performed by this interpretation.

grounding.quote:
Every conserved row
is restated in the receiving member's own text; a route is provenance
only.

concepts.label: Source disposition register

concepts.definition: The Tier-1 EVALUATION member describes justification and acceptance of claims: evidence, independent assessment, review results, acceptance, realisation conformance/equivalence, frame and method qualification, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention. It consumes FOUNDATIONS Results and defines no result values of its own.

grounding.quote: uses; it defines no result values of its own.

concepts.label: EVALUATION

concepts.definition: A load-bearing claim identifies exact subject, claimed property, governing basis, witness-to-claim relation, nearest excluded weaker property and falsifier before witness selection. Absent these, the activity is evidence discovery, not proof.

grounding.quote:
A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof.

concepts.label: Load-bearing claim

grounding.quote:
Every row is one of: derived through an admitted atomic function; derived
through a declared higher-order composition; deferred with an owner and
re-entry condition; excluded by current product authority; or unresolved
as a named gap

constraints.statement: Every discovered-functionality evidence row has exactly a stated disposition: admitted atomic derivation, declared higher-order derivation, deferral with owner and re-entry condition, exclusion by current product authority, or unresolved named gap. Where higher-order behaviour exists, the Ontology names its governing algebra and design states applicable identity, closure, associativity, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws instead of hiding them in controller flow. Iterative discovery of composition, effects and implementation is allowed only when co_evolution_admissible(B) holds; otherwise only a disposable spike supplies evidence across an affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relation before design acceptance. Every retained result is reconciled into accepted design before promotion or design-method closure. No private helper, loop, adapter or endpoint becomes an undeclared constructor.
constraints.uncertainty: The definition of co_evolution_admissible(B) is outside the supplied sections.

grounding.quote:
An atom without a declared admitted domain remains a candidate
atom; it cannot supply Prime acceptance or Prime-conformance to a
realisation projection.

constraints.statement: Smallness, typing, separate naming or independent testability of a file, function, class, record, operation, diagram, module or owner category does not establish Prime. Atomic-function Prime requires complete-family contraction. Every accepted atom declares its admitted domain and governs every admitted instance in it. Later uses compose or parameterise it without local fork, shadow, specialisation or reinterpretation. An out-of-domain case may motivate another candidate for admission; an in-domain counterexample falsifies the shared atom and re-enters its design boundary, not a feature-local replacement. An undeclared domain leaves candidate status and supplies neither Prime acceptance nor projection Prime-conformance.

conditions: Before promotion.

grounding.quote:
A family of individually plausible functions is not Prime when one
parameterised template plus closed variants carries the same meaning and
authority.

constraints.statement: Review asks whether operations are parameters of one function, commands are transitions of one entity, reads are projections of one truth, and implementations are applications of one higher-order function; whether candidates introduce independent identity, authority, effect, lifecycle, reuse or public pattern-match semantics; whether every atom kind entered the same contraction; whether every unit maps explicitly to accepted atoms; and whether any projection introduces, duplicates or reinterprets meaning or authority. A family is not Prime if one parameterised template plus closed variants preserves the same meaning and authority. Visible recurrence is contracted during design; post-implementation recurrence review does not replace this pass.

conditions: At a material semantic boundary.

grounding.quote: Contraction preserves root authority and every retained semantic relation.

constraints.statement: Contract each candidate atom, then the complete resulting family. Local irreducibility or local unit conformance does not prove global Prime where identity, authority, function, lifecycle, topology, effect or projection meaning is duplicated. Preserve root authority and every retained semantic relation; reducing files/functions/operations/authoring surfaces cannot compensate for another authority source or truth path. Evidence states the complete family; each atom's stable identity, irreducible relation, admitted domain and falsifier; whole-family contraction; retained meaning/authority before and after; accepted loss; and total mapping of every proposed projection to accepted atoms. Work inside an accepted boundary cites its existing Prime basis instead of recreating it.

grounding.quote:
If a public operation, sequence message, state transition, carrier or
effect cannot be traced through accepted design to the accepted Ontology,
it is ungrounded design and does not enter the active product line.

constraints.statement: Each design projection identifies its Ontology source and preserved identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority, function or effect law. Intentional omission/flattening declares accepted loss and a failure condition. Target design may add structural HOW but no rival semantic meaning. Implementation and tests trace through accepted design, not around it. Ungrounded public operations, messages, transitions, carriers and effects cannot enter the active product line. Implementation branches and test expectations trace to requirements plus accepted design and preserve the Ontology without needing enumeration there.

grounding.quote:
A top-level realisation unit is Prime-conformant only when it projects one
or more accepted Prime atoms without introducing, duplicating or
reinterpreting semantic authority.

constraints.statement: Derive Prime atoms from a logically complete candidate Ontology before proposing top-level units; whole-family Prime contributes evidence to Ontology acceptance. Target design, IACS, modules, functions, schemas and tests project accepted atoms and do not originate Prime meaning. Typed closure alone does not justify a new top-level type. Prime-conformance requires projection of accepted atoms without introducing, duplicating or reinterpreting semantic authority; topological/effect boundaries first receive atom derivation and acceptance. Typical lawful reasons include new feature topology/work-graph branch, typed-carrier transformation, effect, validation/admission or projection boundary. A unit existing only to shorten a call site without a semantic boundary, aggregate unrelated behaviour, rename an old interface, shuttle through wrappers, hide mutation/fallback/orchestration, name authority-free payload variation, expose internal records, mirror a carrier with slight field differences or relieve typing discomfort by multiplying peers is non-conformant. Prefer composition, existing lawful functions, sharper/fewer boundaries and carrier families; the goal is preventing semantic fragmentation and helper sprawl, not minimising lines.

grounding.quote:
contraction is not
successful when it increases authority centres, maintained truth surfaces,
acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manually reconciled projections
or review burden.

constraints.statement: Apply the referred ACTIVATION §6 proportionality between ambiguity removed and reasoning complexity introduced to Prime contraction. Review cuts, realisation units, runtime modules and work items are distinct boundaries permitting many-to-one or one-to-many relations; administrative convenience does not force one-to-one decomposition. Review counts governance cost as well as implementation count. Increased authority centres, maintained truth surfaces, acceptance boundaries, dependency cycles, manual reconciliation or review burden defeats successful contraction. Evidence remains proportional to semantic change and risk; no artifact or review per concern is required.
constraints.uncertainty: ACTIVATION §6's full proportionality relation is not supplied.

conditions: Defining a schema, carrier family or typed public boundary.

grounding.quote:
7. reconcile the typed implementation to that carrier set before claiming
   design-method closure.

constraints.statement: Derive IACS from accepted Ontology before naming subordinate payloads or implementation modules; it should precede payload records, helper results and internal branch detail. Additional branch payloads, persistence details, read-model rows or typing-oriented field groups do not automatically justify top-level carriers. Required evidence cites accepted Ontology and function derivation, declares IACS, maps every carrier to its identity/lifecycle/function/authority/effect/projection law, marks authoritative versus downstream carriers, defaults all other shapes to subordinate, keeps them private unless Promotion Test passes, and reconciles typed implementation before closure. Without declared accepted Ontology or IACS, the schema is not design-method complete. Under co_evolution_admissible(B), Ontology/evidence/implementation/tests may develop together, but implementation cannot self-ratify newly exposed meaning; Ontology and IACS acceptance and reconciliation precede promotion/closure. Design-gated sequencing accepts affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations before retained implementation establishes them.
constraints.uncertainty: The ASSURANCE binding and co-evolution predicate definitions are not supplied.

conditions: Adding, removing, merging or splitting any carrier.

grounding.quote:
- reruns the Promotion Test and the Boundary Inflation prohibition over
  the full revised set, not only newly introduced carriers;

constraints.statement: IACS is not numerically frozen; revision is lawful through accepted Ontology and design re-entry. Every revision re-derives the whole set and classifies all additions/removals/merges/splits, reapplies Promotion Test and inflation prohibition to the entire set, updates every checker/conformance subject to the declared composite carrier relation under EVALUATION's congruence/freeze/revision law, and reconciles implementation before promotion or closure. A prohibition without lawful revision is false. Revision is false if gates examine only new carriers, assurance keeps a weaker/obsolete subject, or implementation is unreconciled at closure.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §1 is supplied; its §3 freeze/revision law is not.

conditions: Proposing a Subordinate Payload as a top-level type.

grounding.quote: be promoted to a top-level type only when at least one of these is true:

constraints.statement: Promotion requires architectural-boundary justification and at least one of: authoritative source carrier; public/persisted contract boundary; explicit public-outcome variant directly pattern-matched by consumers; reuse across several modules without semantic bleed; independent versioning/publication/admission. These are necessary grounds, not automatic acceptance. Promotion is unlawful for only internal detail of one larger carrier, a once-used field group in one module, temporary typing shim around an open dictionary, private variation crossing no true interface, or cosmetic/local mirror type. Without need for independent authority, independent reuse or direct pattern-match semantics, the shape remains subordinate, nested/private/local. Promotion bears the proof burden; designers/reviewers should assume subordination until an irreducible boundary is shown.

conditions: Schema work; also any schema or ticket listing a wide type family.

grounding.quote:
Typed closure does not excuse Boundary
Inflation.

constraints.statement: Declare IACS, authoritative types, downstream projections, subordinate shapes and subordinate payloads intentionally deferred from promotion. A wide schema/ticket type family must distinguish IACS from subordinate payloads; omission is design drift. Typed closure does not excuse inflation or proliferation into parallel migrations.

conditions: Reference-derived realisation.

grounding.quote:
an
explicit mapping that says what is preserved, reshaped, deferred or
demoted to delivery binding in the target line

constraints.statement: Code comparison alone cannot establish design-method completion. Minimum assets name reference source design surfaces; accepted target Ontology with dispositions for reference entities/functions/lifecycle/authority/effects/projections; target surfaces replacing or binding them; explicit preserved/reshaped/deferred/delivery-demoted mapping; and profile-required module assets including Ontology-derived IACS and the three-view asset. The target boundary and derivation without incidental implementation drift must be demonstrable; otherwise the target is not yet complete.

conditions: Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary.
exceptions: Unchanged boundaries cite accepted basis; local work with no material semantic-boundary delta does not recreate the gate.

grounding.quote:
Every new or materially changed semantic or typed module boundary carries
one accepted Ontology and one complete three-view Mermaid design asset
before the boundary is promoted or claims design-method closure

constraints.statement: One accepted Ontology and a complete three-view design asset precede promotion or design-method closure. Design evidence, implementation and tests may co-develop before that gate only when co_evolution_admissible(B); otherwise acceptance of affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations precedes retained implementation. One broad flowchart does not replace the three models. Views are fidelity-checked Ontology projections, not decoration or peer truth surfaces.

grounding.quote: explicit deferred, excluded and unresolved functionality.

constraints.statement: The asset cites one accepted Ontology for its active boundary and includes/references entity/relationship inventory, invariant/cardinality law, entity-lifecycle completeness matrix, authority matrix, atomic/higher-order derivation matrix, governing composition/effect algebra where applicable, whole-family Prime contraction with every accepted atom's domain and projection mapping, and explicit deferred/excluded/unresolved functionality. A boundary-bounded slice may derive from a wider accepted Ontology only with parent citation and conservation of parent identity, relationship, lifecycle, authority and function law. Copying rows into a local model without that derivation creates another truth surface.

conditions: An accepted material-frame basis and declared bounded action with its causally closed affected set.

grounding.quote:
| preserves | leaves the relation intact and operates inside it | `satisfied` |
| changes | alters the relation itself, and therefore re-enters at that relation before acceptance | `invalid_basis` |
| duplicates | establishes an equivalent path that is explicitly disposed as a constituent, replica, replacement or deliberately independent realisation | `satisfied` |
| violates | contradicts the relation, or establishes an equivalent path that is left undisposed | `falsified` |

constraints.statement: For the predicate 'the action is admissible in the acting frame on the current governing basis', preserves maps to satisfied; changes maps to invalid_basis and requires relation-local re-entry before acceptance; duplicates maps to satisfied only with explicit constituent/replica/replacement/deliberately-independent disposition; violates maps to falsified for contradiction or an undisposed equivalent path. Value travels with predicate and decision. Acceptance locus, not delta size, distinguishes changes from violation: accepting a change inside the acting frame instead of at the changed relation is violation. Disposition, not equivalence, distinguishes lawful duplication. No-decision evaluations return the cause-selected core result, indeterminate when admissible evidence cannot decide and naming what would decide. Inability caused by insufficient method/design evidence falsifies the sufficiency law. Lawful change is neither violation nor locally acceptable; violation is not re-entry.

grounding.quote:
Where the
sufficiency of a boundary is tested, the test uses named cases with known
governing relations and expected decisions, evaluated with conversation
history, commentary, prior-worker memory and implementation folklore
withheld

constraints.statement: Neither selected method nor accepted design substitutes for the other; restating method decision law in design creates prohibited local-method duplication. Sufficiency covers the declared action/affected set, not unbounded future changes, and a particular reviewer's performance is not evidence either way. No additional artifact is required: Ontology evidence, authority matrix, transformation-admission relation, frame declaration, views and module mapping carry the property. The law is false when design omits an affected governing relation or the four-way decision needs conversation, commentary, prior-worker memory or implementation folklore. Tests use named cases with known relations and expected decisions while withholding those informal sources.
constraints.uncertainty: Material-boundary, frame and transformation-admission definitions are referenced outside the supplied sections.

conditions: Active boundary domain view.

grounding.quote:
The standard relationship
expectations are composition for owned subordinate payloads, association
for downstream consumption, and inheritance only for real variant or
outcome families

constraints.statement: Show domain identities/cardinalities rather than helper-class decomposition and all boundary-relevant content identified by the domain-model concept. Standard stereotypes are <<prime-conformant>>, <<subordinate>>, <<effect-edge>>, <<deferred>>, <<authoritative>> and <<downstream>>. Standard visibility is + for public/exported and - for module-local/private. Expected relationships are composition for owned subordinate payloads and association for downstream consumption; inheritance is restricted to real variant/outcome families.

exceptions: Participants may be explicitly external actors rather than domain-model members.

grounding.quote:
Every
message also binds to an Ontology function and its admitted authority
role; actor identity or call reachability alone does not authorise a
message

constraints.statement: Where applicable show malformed inputs/outputs, retry, recursion, fan-out/fan-in, nested workflow and human escalation. Every participant belongs to the domain model or is explicitly external. Every message binds both to a declared carrier transform, graph/computation constructor, interpreter action or effect-handler call and to an Ontology function with admitted authority role. Private loops, methods, plugins, shells or scripts cannot silently replace declared workflow transitions. Actor identity or reachability alone authorises no message.

grounding.quote:
Controller-local memory is not a lawful source of lifecycle truth when the
product declares replay, event, graph or carrier ownership

constraints.statement: Every lifecycle transition binds an Ontology function and names its owning authority, admission, compiler, interpreter, event, projection or external act. When the Product declares replay/event/graph/carrier ownership, controller-local memory cannot supply lifecycle truth.

grounding.quote:
raw probabilistic
output cannot transition directly to accepted or closed

constraints.statement: Evaluation covers every applicable axiom and demonstrates: each view element derives from accepted Ontology; every functionality row has derived/deferred/excluded/gap disposition; every sequence participant and lifecycle carrier exists in the domain model; every message has a declared semantic/effect boundary; every lifecycle transition derives from admitted truth; every function/transition has an explicit authority path with no implicit widening by composition; public operations project Ontology functions; raw probabilistic output cannot become accepted/closed directly; handler/plugin interior ownership requires runtime ownership of admission/events/continuation/closure; native types enforce locally decidable relations; admission/semantic compilation owns global references, completeness and realisation gaps. For graph-native work every batch/retry/recursion/nested workflow is visible in declared graph/compute algebra. A relied-on semantic_not_realized constructor blocks and cannot be replaced by imperative plugin/shell/service/script/test-harness glue.
constraints.uncertainty: The categorical participant requirement differs from the explicit external-actor exception in the sequence-model section.

grounding.quote:
`not_applicable` rests on a false applicability premise, an
unresolved premise supports no `not_applicable`, and the `satisfied` of a
`not_applicable` verdict counts toward this disjunction only, never toward
the predicate that the design meets the axiom:

constraints.statement: The predicate is the disjunction 'on the exact Ontology/design basis, design meets the axiom OR the axiom does not apply'. pass maps to satisfied only when cited Ontology/view/enforcement evidence establishes compliance. not_applicable maps to satisfied only for that disjunction, requires a false applicability premise on basis-bound facts, and names those facts plus the excluding scope authority; it does not establish compliance. fail maps to falsified when applicability holds and an element/message/transition/authority path/enforcement is a counterexample. Record verdict with value. If evaluation reaches no verdict, record the cause-selected core value and what would decide: indeterminate for insufficient admissible evidence, including unresolved applicability with no established compliance; out_of_frame for needed undeclared relation/evaluator capability; invalid_basis for unsupporting Ontology/design basis. An applicable but unevaluated axiom has no result. None is pass; excluded is neither conforming nor failing, and undecided/unevaluated is neither pass nor fail.

conditions: New or semantically changed boundary.

grounding.quote:
an
applicable axiom with no result, or an axiom with no result whose
applicability is not established false, keeps the verdict non-accepted

constraints.statement: Both Ontology and design verdicts must be accepted before promoting affected implementation/public contract/semantic carrier or claiming closure. Failed applicable axioms, missing functionality dispositions, unresolved authority paths and blocking realisation gaps prevent acceptance. Any axiom result other than satisfied, any applicable axiom lacking a result, or a no-result axiom whose applicability is not established false also prevents acceptance. All-pass matrices are evidence, not the authority's verdict; producing the pack establishes neither assessment nor acceptance. Non-accepted means another ACTIVATION disposition or no disposition yet; no disposition means no acceptance result. Missing Ontology, any view, cross-view evaluation or either accepted verdict leaves incompleteness and bars promotion, publication and closure.
constraints.uncertainty: The other three disposition definitions and complete decision-completeness criterion are outside this source slice.

exceptions: An unchanged realization_refactor reuses its existing verdict on accepted-basis citation, touched-projection identification and proof of no entity, relationship, lifecycle, authority, function, effect or public-semantic delta.

grounding.quote:
Until the design gate is accepted it is provisional evidence: it does not
author semantic truth, earn publication authority, or satisfy promotion or
closure.

constraints.statement: Only while co_evolution_admissible(B) holds may implementation precede/co-develop with evidence and be retained after reconciliation; before accepted gate it remains provisional without semantic/publication/promotion/closure authority. Otherwise only a disposable spike crosses affected unresolved, contradictory or materially non-equivalent relations before acceptance. Existing implementation may inform retrospective design, but newly discovered material ambiguity, contradiction or non-equivalent network makes decision_complete(B) false and activates the gate for that decision. Required Ontology, views and axiom evaluation must be accepted before promotion/closure; prior authority evaluates code, not diagrams/Ontology rewritten to rationalise unlawful code. Assets stay boundary-bounded: unrelated bootstrap, harness, projection or delivery shapes added merely for apparent completeness are defects.

grounding.quote:
behaviour
already inside an abstract declared role is ordinary variation; a new
operational responsibility and a new semantic or authoritative role are
each design changes, and only those two require re-entry.

constraints.statement: Every material component declares semantic and operational role sets; multiple roles are lawful but capability creates no authority. Authority-bearing roles preserve applicable authority relations through composition/use. Behaviour within an abstract role is ordinary variation; a new operational responsibility or semantic/authoritative role requires design re-entry. Out-of-role use cannot silently establish identity, admission, lifecycle, ordering, closure or projection truth. Cross-view evaluation extends to prove one system across domain and computational projections. Each material producer-to-consumer path identifies fact establishment, consumers, basis/invalidators, effects, retained alternatives and accumulated work, including material method/assurance operations. Component-local success cannot establish complete-path claims; different names do not prove different computational responsibilities.
constraints.uncertainty: IDENTITY §6, ACTIVATION §§4/7 and ASSURANCE §13 supporting laws are not supplied.

conditions: Material algorithmic work.

grounding.quote: limits and workloads are Product-owned, not universal method constants.

constraints.statement: Declare supported input dimensions, workload/growth and operational assumptions needed for the selected outcome; bind acceptance limits and owning authority before qualification. Product owns limits/workloads. Challenge assumptions on representative supported paths and material growth; observe work directly when elapsed time cannot locate it without repeating operations merely to count them. Existing design/proof surfaces suffice; no new accounting system or fixed complexity is required. Each material algorithmic obligation in M(B) records semantic disposition (existing accepted relation, extension, new candidate) and realisation disposition (consume, implement locally, optimise, adapt, deliberately duplicate under stated non-semantic constraints). Isolation, substrate, performance, security and dependency ownership may justify independent implementation, but an existing accepted relation cannot be presented as newly owned local truth.
constraints.uncertainty: The complete M(B) definition and ACTIVATION §6 cost separation are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
A materially non-equivalent law among
those dimensions requires separation.

constraints.statement: Computational similarity yields a commonisation candidate, then semantic/operational equivalence evaluation, then reuse, a parameterised common relation or justified separation. Shared maps/sequences do not settle identity/key law, ownership, ordering, admissible mutation, consistency/concurrency, retention, failure semantics, access policy, lifecycle or truth authority. Materially non-equivalent law in these dimensions requires separation. Other differences justify separation only when parameterisation/adaptation would weaken ownership, authority, lifecycle, failure or operational constraints; mere difference does not discharge contraction/recurrence review. The law is false for materially equivalent ADTs/algorithms lacking semantic disposition, generic machinery becoming semantic authority, commonisation despite differing identity/ordering/failure/ownership/lifecycle law, or local appropriation of accepted truth.

grounding.quote: This is a theoretical justification, not an extra prerequisite.

constraints.statement: The operational profile stands alone. Its engineering Ontology requires no adoption of world-model domain, Constraint-Emergence Ontology, empirical ontology programme or metaphysical claim. The Markov analogy adds no prerequisite or scope and engineering rules remain applicable when that construct is irrelevant, unavailable or only candidate-class.

exceptions: Typed immutability is recommended unless mutation is materially necessary.

grounding.quote: Convenience is not sufficient justification.

constraints.statement: Source truth should use typed immutable values. Preferred flow is constructor/parser to typed carrier, transformations to another carrier or closed result, and nonmutating projections. Mutable carrier state requires explicit justification for performance-critical use, host-runtime/framework necessity or a genuinely stateful boundary rather than semantic truth. Convenience is insufficient.

exceptions: Totality is qualified by what the language and problem permit; typed explicit failure is preferred when practical.

grounding.quote:
Semantic functions should be total or as close to total as the language
and problem allow

constraints.statement: Semantic functions should be total or as nearly total as allowed, including encounters with inputs outside their admitted domain. Prefer boundary rejection of invalid input, kernels consuming admitted carriers, typed explicit failures where practical, Result-like/closed outcomes, explicit validation and unsupported/rejected outcomes. Avoid hidden-precondition partiality, semantic .get(...) fallback chains and controller reconstruction from defaults. These are recommendations, not universal elimination of exceptions or every imperative construct.

grounding.quote: Effects should be explicit and isolated

constraints.statement: Effects should be explicit and isolated. Typical edges are file writes, network calls, subprocess execution, event append, manifest publication, prompt delivery and database mutation. Kernels should not perform these while deciding law. Prefer admission/parsing of authoritative input, transformation to typed plan/outcome, edge application of effects, then downstream event/projection publication. A function deciding semantic meaning while directly writing should be treated as suspect.

grounding.quote:
Those
meanings should already exist in carriers, contracts or explicit design
modules.

constraints.statement: Controllers, managers, service methods, runtime loops and public wrappers should not hide semantic authority through procedural meaning decisions, fragment-based truth reconstruction, legacy/fallback law rehydration or ad hoc dictionaries/.get chains. A module is an unlawful semantic centre if reading it is necessary to discover closure, identity, failure, next work or current truth; those meanings should already be in carriers, contracts or explicit design modules.

grounding.quote:
`carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections`, not
`controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections`.

constraints.statement: Coupling should be reduced through dependency shape, not file count alone. Preferred source notation is carriers -> semantic kernels -> effect shells -> projections, rather than controllers -> service helpers -> mutable runtime state -> projections. Excess coupling exists when many modules read/mutate one object, projections infer truth from implementation state, consumers silently rebuild truth from raw artifacts, or tests pass only because multiple modules retain the same meaning. Reduction means fewer places capable of inventing meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: Arrow notation is retained as authored; it is not converted into an inferred import direction.

conditions: The boundary governs, observes, routes, audits or evaluates another actor or substrate.
exceptions: Imperative strategy law is allowed only when strategy ownership is explicitly within ratified responsibility.
Assessment budgets/scores/counters/ratings may recreate the actor's judgment only when that assessment boundary is explicitly owned.

grounding.quote:
it publishes governance truth, not
imperative strategy law, unless strategy ownership is explicitly part of
the boundary's ratified responsibility

constraints.statement: Publish governance truth within the boundary's role. Unlawful strategy drift includes downstream repair/action imperatives, framework preferences disguised as observability, unowned assessment heuristics recreating actor judgment, and prompts/reports/read models becoming hidden doctrine. A governance/observability system must not become a replacement decision engine through contexts, projections, prompts or route helpers.

conditions: Lawfully opened realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
Opportunistic
optimisation is lawful only when it is boundary-local to the active design
or module surface; behaviour-preserving at the declared semantic boundary;
authority-neutral, with no change to ownership of truth;
visibility-neutral, with no silent promotion of subordinate payloads; and
effect-neutral, with no hidden expansion of runtime, persistence or
bootstrap doctrine.

constraints.statement: An opened area should be left better, subordinate to constitutional truth, ownership evidence and functional equivalence. Lawful cleanup must be boundary-local, behaviour-preserving, authority-neutral, visibility-neutral and effect-neutral. Cross-module lookup/index/cache/persistence repricing, public-carrier/visibility/ownership changes, wider effects/observability doctrine or performance changes to Product expectations require design re-entry. Cross-boundary opportunities remain repricing input, not silently absorbed work; owner-admitted follow-up enters separately at the smallest lawful point. This profile owns scope separation; TICKETS owns recording and ticket-closure effects. Changed authority, public meaning or cross-boundary doctrine is a new design decision, not cleanup.
constraints.uncertainty: SPEC_METHOD re-entry and TICKETS mechanics are external references.

exceptions: A third local rebuild may be conformant if it consumes an existing reusable surface, extends it before local implementation lands, or review explicitly records do-not-commonise with boundary-specific rationale.

grounding.quote:
a third local rebuild
is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an
existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface
before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit
do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific

constraints.statement: TICKETS §6 owns rule-of-two, third-rebuild threshold, commonisation order and library_usage/governing_library/library_rationale for every implementation migration ticket; this section supplies design-review conformance, not a rival ticket lifecycle. Tenant-local authority-neutral reusable patterns should be extracted under that order. Changing ownership, public carriers, module boundaries or shared law is a separate design decision. Commonisation closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and superseded production responsibility is retired or meets SPEC_METHOD's retention relation. Compare removed work and maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines and unused helpers do not establish contraction.
constraints.uncertainty: Full commonisation ordering and retention criteria are not supplied.

conditions: A processed ticket claims design-method closure under the profile.
exceptions: The check may be normal verification; no separate artifact, review round or reviewer is required.

grounding.quote:
Exact hashes establish subject
identity; headings and artifact presence establish location; green tests
establish only the properties they actually assert.

constraints.statement: Closure should not rest on implementation status alone; check the boundary before closure. Determine lawfulness under current assets, inclusion of every causally applicable live requirement/accepted relation/retained predecessor claim, competing or ambiguous acceptance-path authority, durable architectural decisions foreclosing admitted Product outcomes, and issues falsifying the claim/hard stops. Reconstruct the complete selected function, not merely prior findings; hashes show identity, headings/presence show location and green tests prove only asserted properties. Current accepted Ontology/verdict/reconstruction may be reused only after confirming exact scope, traces, applicability and absence of ACTIVATION §7 invalidators. Source repricing changes the affected basis; later applicable frontier-altering candidates and dominance-defeating evidence/material dimensions change relevant inputs. New role, conversation or review occurrence alone does not invalidate. Missing/stale/ambiguous coverage is not no-delta proof; material changed relations or counterexamples require affected reconstruction/gate while conserving supported unaffected relations.
constraints.uncertainty: The source references three ACTIVATION §7 invalidators but does not enumerate the full external relation.

conditions: A finding arises during the bounded design check.

grounding.quote:
unclaimed future capability and optional clean-up do not become implicit
work.

constraints.statement: A falsifying issue or applicable hard stop blocks design-method closure: falsified does not become satisfied and a hard stop is not waived. Current-promotion blocking is decided by EVALUATION §5; this check's corresponding triggers are falsifying issue, ambiguous/competing acceptance authority, unlawful boundary or omitted causally applicable obligation, and durable architectural foreclosure. Ticket/review wording cannot narrow active authority away. Absorb cleanup/commonisation only when necessary for claim truth, singular authority, accepted design or avoidance of that foreclosure. Other cleanup, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary opportunities are repricing observations that do not automatically enlarge the subject, block its bounded claim or require follow-up tickets. Owner-admitted repricing uses the smallest lawful re-entry. TICKETS retains ticket status/closure/reopening/dependency/follow-up authority. A processed ticket should not claim closure until this check is complete.
constraints.uncertainty: EVALUATION §5 and ticket/re-entry mechanisms are not supplied; closure blocking is not silently equated with every promotion decision.

exceptions: Intentionally retained compatibility is an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof.

grounding.quote:
If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof; otherwise
the proxy path is removed.

Low
coupling requires semantic non-bleed, not only small functions.

constraints.statement: No interface should bleed semantic authority into another family; each family requires one authoritative truth consumed downstream without a new semantic centre. Low coupling requires non-bleed, not just small functions. Proxy or partial interface implementation cannot substitute for real migration or design completion. Absent explicitly owned and proved retained compatibility, remove the proxy path.

conditions: Prompts under this profile.

grounding.quote:
A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour

constraints.statement: Profile prompts follow ACTIVATION §2 prompt construction. A worker may be directed where to inspect and which contract to satisfy. A clause enforcing design law needs provenance and proof that it still causes or prevents its intended behaviour.
constraints.uncertainty: The source attributes this claim to predecessor compression and explicitly says no rc.2 body states it; the underlying prompt-construction law is not supplied.

conditions: Reviewing code under this profile.

grounding.quote: When reviewing code under this profile, ask

constraints.statement: Ask whether: law resides in carriers rather than orchestration; main steps transform admitted truth; effects are isolated; reports cannot invent closure; queries derive admitted truth rather than divergent same-name surfaces; mutation is justified/bounded/local; consumers can pattern-match source carriers; proxies are not silently authoritative; removing the authority carrier fails closed; new functions project accepted atoms without convenience aggregation/rival authority; interfaces do not bleed; Python semantic surfaces avoid Any/open dictionaries/untyped definitions; IACS is declared; subordinate promotions are justified and pass the test; typed closure avoids peer/migration inflation; truth surfaces do not increase and duplicates decrease; foreign/open payloads are not trusted past ingress; enforcement follows proof; governance publishes facts/routes rather than strategy; reference derivation is explicit; domain views show IACS/atom mappings/payloads/visibility/ownership/deferred families; tests derive module ownership/assets; cleanup remains local/preserving/neutral; cross-boundary work has owner admission/re-entry; recurrence has explicit library decisions, including third-rebuild compliance; and closure checks exact claims/hard stops without absorbing optional discoveries.
constraints.uncertainty: These are review questions, not a replacement for conditions and exceptions in the detailed rules.

conditions: Reviewing code under this profile; graph-specific questions retain their graph-profile applicability.

grounding.quote:
Does every Ontology function or transition declare proposer,
    evaluator, verifier, admitter, executor, projector and retirement
    authority as applicable, with actor and capability kept distinct from
    authority?

constraints.statement: Ask whether graph-governed modules realise declared outcome traversals; deterministic boundaries should be declared operative edge traversals; F_D evaluators/transforms/effect shells remain subordinate to GTL/ABG; lifecycle confirmation follows SPEC_METHOD's chain with named Gap:/Unanswered: items; release/deploy/live-use/telemetry/retirement answers come from proper authority; phase non-applicability is reasoned and authority-compatible; domain/sequence/state views are distinct; participants/messages and state transitions are grounded; every applicable axiom is evaluated; relied-on semantic_not_realized constructs block promotion/closure; sequencing is justified and acceptance precedes promotion/closure and design-gated retained implementation; accepted Ontology precedes IACS/public-operation/schema/module/implementation promotion; Ontology enumerates identities, relationships, invariants and complete lifecycle without defaulting to mutable CRUD; applicable proposer/evaluator/verifier/admitter/executor/projector/retirement authorities are declared distinctly from actor/capability; every functionality item is disposed; whole-family Prime covers all atoms/projections/domains; applicable composition/effect laws are proved; all downstream surfaces trace with accepted loss; and removing Ontology would reveal no ungrounded downstream meaning.
constraints.uncertainty: The detailed graph profile, lifecycle chain and earlier authority-model section are not supplied.

conditions: Material generic capability/common-mechanic construction and relevant foundation selection.

grounding.quote:
Did any newly exposed material generic subproblem recursively re-enter
    the foundation-selection relation before its implementation was
    retained?

constraints.statement: Ask whether the generic capability is stated without Product/domain/module/vendor/file/incumbent labels and separates declared semantic/authority relations from mechanics; bounded discovery records every searched source/category, cutoff time/version basis, applicability criteria, exclusions, predecessor/incumbent status and residual unknown, with later material candidates invalidating affected selection; credible compositions are compared over decision-relevant lifecycle dimensions without incumbent/source-order/local-code/dependency-count preference; hard authority/Product-contract/safety/security/licensing/constructability failures eliminate candidates while unknowns remain explicit; reused foundations hold only assigned roles preserving owner, role kind, subject, scope, basis, lifecycle and refusal invariants; selection is undominated under evidence with existing trade-off owner applying declared priorities/risk tolerance rather than undefined total order; every material rejection has decisive evidence/falsifier and unresolved frontier stays a gap; and newly exposed material generic subproblems re-enter selection before retained implementation.
constraints.uncertainty: UP-023's full candidate sources, comparison dimensions and selection relation are outside this slice.

conditions: The project claims the functional properties identified by the checklist.

grounding.quote:
- [ ] defaults are explicit, ratified and carrier-owned rather than
      helper-owned;

constraints.statement: Explicitly check constitutional WHAT preservation and lawful HOW; one accepted Ontology deriving all semantic kinds; every create/read/update/retire lifecycle question mapped to lawful function, reasoned not_applicable or owned gap; distinct authority/capability/actor roles; complete functionality disposition with no verb-to-operation shortcut; pre-promotion contraction, domains and atom/projection mappings; fidelity of IACS/views/contracts/adapters/code/tests; reference equivalence and reference-to-target-to-module mapping before implementation where a reference exists; proportional foundation selection before material generic construction with discovery/frontier/roles/evidence; implementation and tests from the same module assets; singular owners and reduced duplicate/reconstructed truth; admitted inputs and pure functions; no time/randomness/UUID/environment/process/filesystem/network/global-registry dependence in the semantic centre; explicitly owned ingress/effect identity creation; immutable new-value carriers and no shared mutable semantic state; direct transforms without parser/validator/loader re-entry on locally assembled truth; ingress rejection rather than procedural repair; explicit ratified carrier-owned defaults; one function owner/responsibility separating admission, semantics and effects; algebra depending on carrier contracts rather than shells, admission on validation rather than orchestration; no meaning-deciding effectful function; explicit typed effect edges that cannot erase carriers into open objects; subordinate bootstrap/controller/adapter/runtime layers; and governance facts/eligibility/provenance without imperative builder strategy.
constraints.uncertainty: The checklist's categorical purity/immutability language is retained as a claim-triggered check; its interaction with general mutation exceptions is not silently resolved.

conditions: Functional-property review; hard-gate subset for new or materially changed boundaries.
exceptions: For an unchanged boundary, accepted basis plus no-material-semantic-delta evidence suffices without new Ontology, IACS, views, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane.

grounding.quote:
For an unchanged boundary, the hard gate is the accepted basis plus
evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not require a new
Ontology, IACS, three-view asset, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane

constraints.statement: Also explicitly check current complete domain/sequence/state views, axiom matrix and accepted verdict without bypassed gaps; module/IACS-derived tests; bounded preserving/neutral cleanup; explicit recurrence decisions, consumption/extension of available common surfaces or boundary-specific/not-yet-lawful rationale; owner-admitted cross-boundary work; bounded closure check; negative proof that imperative/open-payload/effect-erasure bypass fails closed; graph-profile modules inside declared outcome traversal and repricing where they decide next work, closure, semantic target movement or graph-function identity; lifecycle confirmation with answers, reasoned non-applicability or named gaps; and operational claims grounded in Product/requirement/design/release/operational authority. The new/material hard gate requires accepted Ontology at promotion/closure and earlier for design-gated unresolved/contradictory/non-equivalent choices; lifecycle/authority/function evidence; whole-family Prime, domains, mappings and algebras; proportional capability selection with discovery/frontier/role conservation; pure semantic functions, immutable carriers, no shared mutation, one truth owner, low coupling, no hidden runtime authority; accepted three views; complete axiom evaluation/no bypass; semantic equivalence to specification and any reference; lifecycle confirmation/gaps; and negative imperative/open-bypass proof. The checklist applies across languages.
constraints.uncertainty: The checklist says Mermaid categorically while the main gate allows ratified equivalent text-native formats.

conditions: The profile is adopted across a named boundary.

grounding.quote:
When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane

constraints.statement: Apply the profile consistently to Ontology/architecture derivation, design modules, runtime/execution kernels, prompt/reporting paths, constructors/materialisers and projection/query surfaces. Carrier/schema/governance migrations should make boundary closure evaluators explicit in ADR/ticket. Every new/materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares/cites accepted Ontology before completion, with lifecycle, authority, function derivation, whole-family Prime, domains, mappings and traces proportional to the change. Schema/typed-carrier changes derive and reconcile IACS before completion. Reference-derived changes publish reference-to-target and Ontology-derived three-view assets before completion. Active implementation of new/material changes publishes a module-derived test lane before closure.
constraints.uncertainty: Adoption's Product-authority replacement is explicitly proposed and pending owner acceptance in the source disposition register; no acceptance is inferred.

grounding.quote:
It does not decide release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector
promotion, install policy or operational rollout

constraints.statement: For graph-governed Products, the graph profile decides whether the operative unit is outcome traversal, graph function, GTL module or ABG runtime boundary; DESIGN_MODULE governs deterministic structure realising/evaluating/adapting/projecting inside it. UX is loaded only for UX work and adds render/reducer purity, effect membrane and AssetSurface bindings. ASSURANCE lifecycle confirmation determines sufficient lifecycle signal for safe build/review, not release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector promotion, install policy or rollout, which remain RELEASE/project-owned. The taxonomy's design-to-module evidence route, module-derived tests and lifecycle confirmation belong to ASSURANCE §§14–16 through the profile's declared binding.
constraints.uncertainty: Referenced members and the binding at the document head are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type

constraints.statement: The profile requires neither a specific language, elimination of all imperative code, monadic/category-theory vocabulary nor replacement of every exception with a custom algebraic type. These non-goals do not remove the composition/effect algebra requirement where higher-order/effectful computation is composed; implementation-shape law is referred to SPEC_METHOD §2.
constraints.uncertainty: The full implementation readability/shape requirement is not supplied.

grounding.quote:
The predecessor's "must" is
written in the indicative; every "should", "may", "recommended",
"typical", "preferred", "normally", "usually", "minimum", "where
practical" and "allowed" keeps its force.

constraints.statement: The register routes predecessor anchors to receiving loci and claims conserved rows are restated, while routes alone are provenance. Its renamings map SPEC_METHOD/RELEASE_METHOD/TICKET_METHOD/UX_METHOD to tenant members; ODD terminology to graph profile retaining GTL/ABG/F_D/graph function/edge traversal; UP-021 to ACTIVATION §4, UP-022 to EVALUATION §§1/3, UP-004 to IDENTITY §6; Agentic Construction Execution to ACTIVATION §1; lifecycle sufficiency to SPEC_METHOD §2; interface migration/retention to SPEC_METHOD §7; world model to its profile; method/basis/constructor and section names to successor terminology. Indicative wording carries predecessor must, while should/may/recommended/typical/preferred/normally/usually/minimum/where-practical/allowed retain their force. Existing higher-tier law is referenced rather than repeated. Register rows claim conservation of the supplied rules and routing of assurance rules to ASSURANCE §§14–16; they do not independently prove conservation.
constraints.uncertainty: Predecessor documents and many receiving loci are not included.

grounding.quote:
a passing check of a necessary condition establishes that
condition and no more

constraints.statement: Before witness selection, name subject, property, governing basis, witness relation, excluded nearest weaker property and falsifier; otherwise there is discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax, compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claims merely because easier to measure. Recursive/repeated-construction claims state preservation, progress, termination or outcome satisfaction. The witness assertion states whether its predicate is the full obligation, a necessary condition or part of a sufficient conjunction; expected result has assertion provenance and execution has execution provenance. A passing necessary condition establishes only that condition.
constraints.uncertainty: External construction and provenance definitions are not supplied.

conditions: Assurance supports promotion or closure; mechanical-enforcement claims retain their additional conditions.

grounding.quote:
a planned or
specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,
and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim
remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property

constraints.statement: Every checker, validator, harness, reviewer or assurance surface binds the exact claimed subject and authoritative composition relation. File/carrier evidence proves only that boundary; cross-carrier satisfaction/conflict is decided at the declared composite boundary. Mechanical enforcement names an executable/reproducible predicate and a witness reachable through the ordinary declared assurance path. Until both predicate and reachable witness are observed, the claim stays open or is explicitly downgraded to planned evidence; a specification-only/planned harness is not observed verification.

grounding.quote:
Later counterevidence
invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is
superseded, withdrawn or requalified

constraints.statement: Claim quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed evaluated evidence. Generalising local defects/observations requires declared inference relation, comparable population, counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is superseded, withdrawn or requalified. Quantifier/boundary rules are false when assurance observes weaker/different subjects, per-carrier evidence closes an unevaluated composite, enforcement lacks predicate/reachable witness, plans are reported as observations, verdicts exceed evaluated population/inference or survive material counterevidence without requalification.

Retains material-change gate, unchanged exemption and conditional formatting latitude.
Retains required inventories and parent-slice conservation.

Retains structural content, stereotypes, visibility and relationship expectations.
